beats.visual: A tomato sitting on a kitchen counter with a red stamp reading COOKED WRONG
beats.label: COOKED WRONG
beats.narration: Right now, there is a vegetable in your kitchen that you have been cooking wrong.

beats.visual: A tomato with its goodness spilling out through a hole in the bottom
beats.label: MOST OF IT WASTED
beats.narration: Not slightly wrong. Wrong in a way that throws away most of the benefit.

beats.visual: A health tips board with the rule crossed out and a reversing arrow
beats.label: THE OPPOSITE
beats.narration: And the fix is the opposite of what every health account has told you.

beats.visual: A cookbook page reading cooking destroys nutrients with a big red X
beats.label: THE RULE YOU KNOW
beats.narration: You have been told for years that cooking destroys nutrients in vegetables.

beats.visual: The same rule page flipped upside down with a backwards arrow
beats.label: BACKWARDS
beats.narration: For this one vegetable, that rule is not just wrong, it is backwards.

beats.visual: A scientist with a pan of tomatoes beside a rack of blood sample tubes
beats.label: MEASURED IN BLOOD
beats.narration: Researchers cooked tomatoes and measured exactly what happened in human blood afterward.

beats.visual: A blood tube with lycopene molecules rising and a gauge climbing
beats.narration: The amount of lycopene in their blood rose by eighty two percent.

beats.visual: Two pans side by side, one with oil rising, one flat lining
beats.label: ONLY WITH FAT
beats.narration: But only when they cooked it with fat. Without fat, nothing happened at all.

beats.visual: A completely flat graph line stamped NO SIGNIFICANT INCREASE
beats.label: FLAT LINE
beats.narration: The group that cooked tomatoes without oil showed no significant increase whatsoever.

beats.visual: A document with an official randomised controlled trial stamp on it
beats.label: NOT A DIET BOOK
beats.narration: That is not a diet book claim. That is a randomised controlled trial.

beats.visual: A finger pointing at a big bold number with a question mark beside it
beats.label: STAY FOR THE NUMBER
beats.narration: Stay until the end, because I will show you the exact number.

beats.visual: Two warning triangles labelled mistake one and mistake two
beats.label: TWO MISTAKES
beats.narration: And the two mistakes that almost everyone makes with this single vegetable.

beats.visual: A pile of vegetables with a person shrugging beside it
beats.label: NOT ABOUT EATING MORE
beats.narration: This is not about eating more vegetables. You probably already eat enough.

beats.visual: Vegetables travelling down a tube toward a bloodstream, some bouncing off
beats.label: DOES IT REACH YOU
beats.narration: This is about whether the vegetables you eat actually reach your bloodstream.

beats.visual: Two doors, one reading swallowed and one absorbed, only one open
beats.label: SWALLOWED VS ABSORBED
beats.narration: Because there is a difference between swallowing a nutrient and absorbing it.

beats.visual: A finish line labelled the swallow with the science starting just behind
beats.label: WHERE ADVICE STOPS
beats.narration: Most health advice stops at the swallow. The science starts after it.

beats.visual: Three numbered boxes on a hand drawn title card
beats.label: WHAT'S COMING
beats.narration: Here is what I am going to show you, and it is genuinely simple.

beats.visual: A tomato cut open revealing a hidden glowing molecule inside
beats.label: THE HIDDEN COMPOUND
beats.narration: First, the compound hiding inside tomatoes that almost nobody talks about properly.

beats.visual: Two big red X marks over everyday cooking habits
beats.label: THE MISTAKES
beats.narration: Second, the two everyday mistakes that throw most of that compound away.

beats.visual: A body outline with the compound glowing as it travels inside
beats.label: WHAT IT DOES
beats.narration: Third, what it measurably does once it is actually inside your body.

beats.visual: A hand holding a tomato beside a checklist of numbered steps
beats.label: THE EXACT WAY
beats.narration: And I will give you the exact way to eat it, with real numbers.

beats.visual: Supplement bottles and powder tubs crossed out, one tomato highlighted
beats.label: NOT A SUPPLEMENT
beats.narration: Not a supplement, not a powder, not a bottle with a label.

beats.visual: A tomato with a tick and the word free stamped across it
beats.label: ALREADY YOURS
beats.narration: The tomato you already own, prepared in a way you have probably never tried.

beats.visual: A person at a table looking thoughtfully at a single tomato
beats.label: LAST TIME
beats.narration: Think about the last time you ate a tomato. Really think about it.

beats.visual: A sliced raw tomato on a salad plate, cold and firm
beats.label: RAW ON A SALAD
beats.narration: Maybe it was sliced raw on a salad, cold and firm and slightly sour.

beats.visual: A hand eating cherry tomatoes straight from a punnet
beats.label: STRAIGHT FROM THE PUNNET
beats.narration: Maybe it was a few cherry tomatoes eaten straight from the punnet while cooking.

beats.visual: A jar of pasta sauce with a spoon resting in it
beats.label: FROM A JAR
beats.narration: Or maybe it was already cooked, in a pasta sauce from a jar.

beats.visual: A person giving a thumbs up beside a tomato with a halo
beats.label: TOMATOES ARE HEALTHY
beats.narration: You probably felt good about it. Tomatoes are healthy, everyone agrees on that.

beats.visual: A magnifying glass over a small hidden detail on a healthy tomato
beats.label: WHY IT'S MISSED
beats.narration: And they are. That is exactly why this is so easy to miss.

beats.visual: A rule book with one rule highlighted and no source cited
beats.label: ONE UNQUESTIONED RULE
beats.narration: Because we have absorbed one rule without ever questioning where it came from.

beats.visual: Three rule cards, fresh, raw and cooking destroys, stacked up
beats.label: THE THREE RULES
beats.narration: Fresh is better. Raw is better. Cooking destroys nutrients. End of discussion.

beats.visual: A vitamin C molecule shrinking away in a hot pan
beats.label: TRUE FOR VITAMIN C
beats.narration: That rule is true for vitamin C. Cooking really does destroy it.

beats.visual: A timer at thirty minutes with vitamin C dropping twenty nine percent
beats.label: MINUS 29%
beats.narration: Cook one for thirty minutes and you lose twenty nine percent of its vitamin C.

beats.visual: A tick mark beside a measured loss on a chart
beats.label: RULE CONFIRMED
beats.narration: So the rule feels confirmed. You measured the loss and you were right.

beats.visual: A vitamin C badge crossed out, a lycopene molecule glowing larger beside it
beats.label: NOT THE REAL REASON
beats.narration: But vitamin C is not the real reason tomatoes are worth eating.

beats.visual: A pan on heat with a rising arrow inside the tomato itself
beats.label: SOMETHING WAS RISING
beats.narration: In that same thirty minutes, something else inside the tomato was increasing.

beats.visual: A big number one hundred sixty four percent with a red pigment molecule rising
beats.label: PLUS 164%
beats.narration: The compound that makes tomatoes red went up by one hundred sixty four percent.

beats.visual: An antioxidant meter climbing sixty two percent above a pan
beats.label: PLUS 62%
beats.narration: Total antioxidant activity in that same pan rose by sixty two percent.

beats.visual: A see-saw with vitamin C going down and lycopene going up
beats.label: DOWN AND UP
beats.narration: The vitamin went down, but the thing that actually matters went up.

beats.visual: A person stopping with a hand to ear, a speech bubble reading sounds like a trick
beats.label: SOUNDS LIKE A TRICK
beats.narration: That is the moment most people stop listening, because it sounds like a trick.

beats.visual: A chemistry flask with a tick, a magician's hat crossed out
beats.label: JUST CHEMISTRY
beats.narration: It is not a trick. It is chemistry, and it is very easy to understand.

beats.visual: A tomato wearing a name tag reading lycopene
beats.label: LYCOPENE
beats.narration: The red pigment in a tomato has a name. It is called lycopene.

beats.visual: A molecule labelled carotenoid beside an empty vitamin bottle crossed out
beats.label: A CAROTENOID
beats.narration: Lycopene is not a vitamin. It is a carotenoid, a pigment molecule.

beats.visual: A lycopene molecule on a podium among antioxidant contestants
beats.label: HIGHLY EFFICIENT
beats.narration: And it is one of the most efficient antioxidants found anywhere in nature.

beats.visual: Lycopene defeating ten free radical monsters while vitamin E handles one
beats.label: TEN TIMES
beats.narration: It neutralises more than ten times the free radicals that vitamin E handles.

beats.visual: A lycopene crystal locked inside a cage of plant cell walls
beats.label: LOCKED INSIDE
beats.narration: But inside a raw tomato, lycopene is locked in a crystalline prison.

beats.visual: A padlocked crystal behind thick brick cell walls
beats.label: YOUR GUT CAN'T OPEN IT
beats.narration: It sits inside rigid cell walls, packed in crystals your gut cannot open.

beats.visual: A safe with a welded door and banknotes visible through the gap
beats.label: A WELDED SAFE
beats.narration: Picture a safe with the door welded shut. The money is still inside.

beats.visual: The safe with everything valuable trapped behind the welded door
beats.label: TRAPPED
beats.narration: Everything of value is there, and none of it can get out to help you.

beats.visual: A person swallowing a whole safe instead of opening the door
beats.label: SWALLOWING THE SAFE
beats.narration: Eating that tomato raw is like swallowing the safe instead of opening it.

beats.visual: Fibre, water and vitamin C passing through, lycopene bouncing away
beats.label: STRAIGHT THROUGH
beats.narration: You get the fibre, the water, the vitamin C. The lycopene passes right through.

beats.visual: A flame cracking rigid plant cell walls open like a nutcracker
beats.label: HEAT OPENS IT
beats.narration: Heat is what opens the safe. It breaks those rigid plant cell walls apart.

beats.visual: A surprised scientist with a shaking clipboard and an unexpected result
beats.label: SOMETHING ELSE
beats.narration: And it does something else that nobody expected when they first measured it.

beats.visual: Two lycopene molecules, one straight one bent, labelled trans and cis
beats.label: TRANS AND CIS
beats.narration: Lycopene comes in two shapes, straight and bent. Scientists call them trans and cis.

beats.visual: A bent cis molecule slipping through the intestinal wall, the straight one stuck
beats.label: BENT ABSORBS BETTER
beats.narration: Your body absorbs the bent cis form far more easily than the straight one.

beats.visual: Heat flipping straight molecules into bent ones like pancakes
beats.label: HEAT FLIPS THEM
beats.narration: Cooking flips a meaningful share of the straight molecules into the bent shape.

beats.visual: One worker doing two jobs at once, freeing and reshaping
beats.label: TWO JOBS
beats.narration: So heat does two jobs at once. It frees the lycopene and reshapes it.

beats.visual: A staircase with step one marked and a warning sign further up
beats.label: STEP ONE ONLY
beats.narration: But freeing it is only step one, and this is where most people still fail.

beats.visual: Lycopene refusing to mix with water, dissolving happily in oil
beats.label: FAT SOLUBLE
beats.narration: Lycopene does not dissolve in water. It dissolves in fat, and only fat.

beats.visual: Lycopene molecules boarding transport particles made of fat
beats.label: THE TRANSPORT
beats.narration: Your intestine absorbs it by packaging it into particles built from dietary fat.

beats.visual: A lycopene molecule with no vehicle watching the transport drive past
beats.label: NO TRANSPORT
beats.narration: No fat in the meal means no transport. The freed lycopene simply keeps going.

beats.visual: Twenty three people lined up in a trial room
beats.label: 23 PEOPLE
beats.narration: This was not assumed. It was tested directly on twenty three people.

beats.visual: Two tables, one with an olive oil bottle and one without
beats.label: TWO GROUPS
beats.narration: One group ate tomatoes cooked with olive oil. One group ate them without.

beats.visual: A blood chart with the olive oil group climbing eighty two percent
beats.label: PLUS 82%
beats.narration: The group that had olive oil saw their blood lycopene rise by eighty two percent.

beats.visual: A flat line graph stamped no significant increase
beats.label: NOT EVEN SMALL
beats.narration: The group without oil showed no significant increase. Not a small one.

beats.visual: A statistics board reading P equals zero point six eight four
beats.label: P = 0.684
beats.narration: Nothing. The statistical result was a P value of zero point six eight four.

beats.visual: A plain language translation bubble reading as close to nothing as possible
beats.label: IN PLAIN TERMS
beats.narration: In plain terms, that is as close to no effect as research can report.

beats.visual: Two mistake boxes stacked on top of each other
beats.label: THEY STACK
beats.narration: So there are two mistakes, and they stack on top of each other.

beats.visual: A hand eating a raw tomato with lycopene still locked in cells
beats.label: MISTAKE ONE
beats.narration: Eat it raw and you never free the lycopene from the plant cells.

beats.visual: A pan with no oil, freed molecules escaping upward unabsorbed
beats.label: MISTAKE TWO
beats.narration: Cook it without fat and you free it, then fail to absorb it.

beats.visual: A single mistake knocking most of the benefit off a scale
beats.label: EITHER ONE IS ENOUGH
beats.narration: Either mistake on its own is enough to lose most of the benefit.

beats.visual: A big glowing number beside a video play button
beats.label: THE NUMBER
beats.narration: Now the number that convinced me this was worth a whole video.

beats.visual: Two plates holding the exact same measured dose of lycopene
beats.label: SAME DOSE
beats.narration: Researchers gave people the exact same dose of lycopene two different ways.

beats.visual: Raw tomatoes on one side, tomato paste on the other, both with oil
beats.label: FRESH VS PASTE
beats.narration: Once from raw fresh tomatoes, once from processed tomato paste. Both with fat.

beats.visual: A clock with blood samples being taken hour after hour
beats.label: MEASURED FOR HOURS
beats.narration: Then they measured the lycopene actually appearing in their blood over hours.

beats.visual: A bar chart with the paste peak towering two and a half times higher
beats.label: 2.5 TIMES
beats.narration: The paste group hit a peak two and a half times higher than fresh.

beats.visual: An area chart showing nearly four times the shaded absorption
beats.label: NEARLY 4X
beats.narration: Across the whole window they absorbed nearly four times more in total.

beats.visual: Three identical labels, same food, same dose, same fat
beats.label: SAME EVERYTHING
beats.narration: Same food. Same dose. Same fat. Almost four times the amount absorbed.

beats.visual: A journal cover reading American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 1997
beats.label: AJCN 1997
beats.narration: That study was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 1997.

beats.visual: The same person swapping between two groups with a crossover arrow
beats.label: CROSSOVER TRIAL
beats.narration: It was a crossover trial, so every participant served as their own control.

beats.visual: A magnifying glass over one small detail in the data table
beats.label: THE TELL
beats.narration: And here is the detail that tells you this is real and specific.

beats.visual: Other carotenoid molecules being measured alongside the lycopene
beats.label: THEY CHECKED OTHERS
beats.narration: They also measured the other carotenoids present in those same blood samples.

beats.visual: Alpha and beta carotene each with a flat line graph
beats.label: THE OTHERS FLAT
beats.narration: Alpha carotene and beta carotene both showed no significant difference at all.

beats.visual: A crystal structure with a target on it, everything else greyed out
beats.label: SPECIFIC TO LYCOPENE
beats.narration: The effect was specific to lycopene and the crystal structure it sits in.

beats.visual: A real finding badge beside a crumpled nutrition headline
beats.label: REAL VS HEADLINE
beats.narration: That specificity is what separates a real finding from a nutrition headline.

beats.visual: A researcher with wide eyes and a clipboard slipping from their hands
beats.label: SURPRISED THEM TOO
beats.narration: Now here is the part that surprised even the researchers who ran it.

beats.visual: A body map with lycopene gathering unevenly in specific organs
beats.label: IT PICKS SPOTS
beats.narration: Lycopene does not float around evenly once it is in your body.

beats.visual: A cross-section of skin with lycopene molecules settling into it
beats.label: YOUR SKIN
beats.narration: It accumulates in specific tissues, and one of them is your skin.

beats.visual: A research team pointing at an impossible looking question mark
beats.label: SOUNDS IMPOSSIBLE
beats.narration: So a team of researchers decided to test something that sounds impossible.

beats.visual: Sun rays hitting an arm with a question mark and a tomato beside it
beats.label: FOOD AS SUNBLOCK
beats.narration: Could eating a food change how badly your skin burns in sunlight?

beats.visual: Nine volunteers each eating forty grams of tomato paste daily
beats.label: 40G A DAY
beats.narration: Nine volunteers ate forty grams of tomato paste every day for ten weeks.

beats.visual: A spoon of tomato paste labelled sixteen milligrams beside olive oil
beats.label: 16 MG
beats.narration: That is about sixteen milligrams of lycopene, always eaten with olive oil.

beats.visual: Ten other people with olive oil only and an empty tomato paste bowl
beats.label: THE CONTROL GROUP
beats.narration: Ten other people ate the same olive oil and no tomato paste at all.

beats.visual: A solar simulator lamp shining UV onto a patch of back skin
beats.label: CONTROLLED UV
beats.narration: Then researchers shone a controlled dose of ultraviolet light on their skin.

beats.visual: Two skin patches side by side, one clearly forty percent less red
beats.label: 40% LESS RED
beats.narration: The tomato paste group developed forty percent less redness than the control group.

beats.visual: A big forty percent badge with a sun and a tomato together
beats.label: FORTY PERCENT
beats.narration: Forty percent less sunburn, measured, from eating a food for ten weeks.

beats.visual: A journal cover reading Journal of Nutrition, 2001
beats.label: J NUTR 2001
beats.narration: That study ran in the Journal of Nutrition in two thousand and one.

beats.visual: Twenty women in a twelve week randomised trial calendar
beats.label: REPEATED
beats.narration: A later randomised trial repeated it in twenty women over twelve weeks.

beats.visual: Skin layers with protection shields at two different depths
beats.label: DEEPER DAMAGE TOO
beats.narration: It found protection not just from redness, but from deeper damage too.

beats.visual: A skin matrix grid and a mitochondrial DNA strand both shielded
beats.label: MATRIX AND DNA
beats.narration: Changes in the skin's structural matrix, and damage to mitochondrial DNA itself.

beats.visual: An honest weighing scale with a hand holding one side down
beats.label: BEING HONEST
beats.narration: Now I need to be completely honest with you about the scale here.

beats.visual: A tiny SPF one point three badge beside a huge SPF thirty bottle
beats.label: SPF 1.3
beats.narration: That protection works out to roughly an SPF of one point three.

beats.visual: A dermatologist pointing at SPF thirty, tomato paste crossed out as sunscreen
beats.label: NOT SUNSCREEN
beats.narration: Dermatologists recommend a factor of thirty or higher. This is not sunscreen.

beats.visual: A small shield growing slowly across a calendar of months
beats.label: SLOW AND SMALL
beats.narration: It is a small basal layer of protection that builds slowly over months.

beats.visual: A calendar showing week four no difference and week ten protection
beats.label: TEN WEEKS
beats.narration: And it took ten weeks to appear. At week four there was no difference.

beats.visual: A cardiologist with a heart and a blood pressure cuff
beats.label: THE HEART ANGLE
beats.narration: There is a third thing, and it is the one cardiologists care about.

beats.visual: Six trial documents being pooled into one analysis
beats.label: SIX TRIALS
beats.narration: A pooled analysis of six controlled trials looked directly at blood pressure.

beats.visual: A blood pressure gauge with the systolic number dropping about five points
beats.label: MINUS 5 MMHG
beats.narration: Systolic pressure dropped by an average of about five millimetres of mercury.

beats.visual: A blood pressure reading with the top number highlighted beside stiff arteries
beats.label: THE TOP NUMBER
beats.narration: That is the top number, the one that rises as arteries stiffen.

beats.visual: A high gauge improving while a normal gauge stays flat
beats.label: ONLY IF ELEVATED
beats.narration: But it only appeared in people whose blood pressure was already elevated.

beats.visual: A normal blood pressure gauge stamped no change
beats.label: NOT IF YOU'RE NORMAL
beats.narration: In people with already normal pressure, lycopene did essentially nothing at all.

beats.visual: A signpost pointing to exactly who this helps
beats.label: WHO IT'S FOR
beats.narration: Which is honest and useful, because it tells you who this is actually for.

beats.visual: A dose scale with twelve milligrams marked as the threshold
beats.label: ABOVE 12 MG
beats.narration: Daily doses above twelve milligrams worked noticeably better than the smaller doses.

beats.visual: A title card with four numbered boxes in hand drawn capitals
beats.label: FOUR STEPS
beats.narration: So what do you actually do with all of this? Four things.

beats.visual: Step one card beside a pan of tomatoes cooking properly
beats.label: STEP ONE: COOK THEM
beats.narration: Simple, specific, and all of them free. Step one, cook your tomatoes.

beats.visual: A pan with tomatoes breaking down gently, a boiling pot crossed out
beats.label: IN A PAN
beats.narration: Not boiled to death. Cooked properly, in a pan, until they break down.

beats.visual: A timer at twenty to thirty minutes beside a rising graph
beats.label: 20 TO 30 MINUTES
beats.narration: Twenty to thirty minutes is where the research found the biggest increase.

beats.visual: Step two card with olive oil pouring into the pan
beats.label: STEP TWO: ADD FAT
beats.narration: Step two, cook them with fat. Olive oil is the obvious choice.

beats.visual: A fat free pan with freed molecules escaping upward and away
beats.label: FREED THEN LOST
beats.narration: Without fat in the same meal, you free the lycopene and lose it.

beats.visual: A chemistry flask with a tick, a chef's hat crossed out
beats.label: CHEMISTRY, NOT OPINION
beats.narration: This is genuine chemistry, not a preference and not a chef's opinion.

beats.visual: Step three card with tomato paste, passata and tinned tomatoes on a shelf
beats.label: STEP THREE: PROCESSED
beats.narration: Step three, choose processed tomato products when you can. Paste, passata, tinned.

beats.visual: Tomato paste on a podium ahead of fresh tomatoes, four to one
beats.label: PASTE WINS
beats.narration: The paste in the absorption study beat fresh tomatoes by nearly four times.

beats.visual: A marketing megaphone crossed out beside a blood sample with a tick
beats.label: MEASURED, NOT MARKETED
beats.narration: That is not marketing talk. It was measured directly in human blood.

beats.visual: A tin of tomatoes and a jar of passata both with ticks
beats.label: TINNED COUNTS
beats.narration: Tinned tomatoes count too, and so does a decent jar of passata.

beats.visual: Step four card with a tomato half raw and half cooked
beats.label: STEP FOUR: EAT BOTH
beats.narration: Step four, keep eating some raw as well. This is not either or.

beats.visual: A raw tomato wearing a vitamin C badge
beats.label: KEEP THE VITAMIN C
beats.narration: Raw tomatoes still give you the vitamin C that cooking partly destroys.

beats.visual: Two plates side by side, cooked with fat and raw, both ticked
beats.label: BOTH
beats.narration: So eat both. Cooked with fat for lycopene, raw for the vitamin C.

beats.visual: A salad with raw tomato and olive oil beside a bowl of cooked sauce
beats.label: ONE DAY, BOTH WAYS
beats.narration: A salad with raw tomato and olive oil, plus a cooked sauce at dinner.

beats.visual: One plate covering both compounds with two satisfied ticks
beats.label: TWO COMPOUNDS COVERED
beats.narration: That single combination covers both compounds without you thinking about it again.

beats.visual: A calendar with ten weeks marked and a slow moving turtle
beats.label: A LONG GAME
beats.narration: And if you want the skin effect, understand it is a long game.

beats.visual: A beach holiday one week away crossed out, ten weeks ticked
beats.label: NOT A QUICK FIX
beats.narration: Ten weeks of daily intake. Not a week before a beach holiday.

beats.visual: A tall stack of published nutrition papers on a desk
beats.label: IT'S ALL PUBLISHED
beats.narration: All of this is sitting in the published nutrition literature right now.

beats.visual: A research paper on one side, a home kitchen on the other, a wide gap
beats.label: THE GAP
beats.narration: But almost nobody translates it into something you can use in a kitchen.

beats.visual: A bridge labelled Food Code spanning from the paper to the pan
beats.label: THE MISSION
beats.narration: That gap between the paper and your pan is what Food Code is for.

beats.visual: A person transformed, glowing brain, looking thoughtfully at a tomato
beats.label: YOU CHANGED
beats.narration: After today you are not someone who just eats tomatoes because they are healthy.

beats.visual: A name tag on a red pigment molecule and a locked crystal
beats.label: YOU KNOW ITS NAME
beats.narration: You know the pigment has a name, and you know it is locked inside.

beats.visual: Heat cracking cell walls and flipping molecules into bent shapes
beats.label: YOU KNOW THE MECHANISM
beats.narration: You know heat opens the walls and flips the molecule into its bent shape.

beats.visual: A fat transport truck carrying lycopene, an empty road without it
beats.label: YOU KNOW THE TRANSPORT
beats.narration: You know fat is the transport, and without it the whole thing is wasted.

beats.visual: A raw tomato stamped not automatically better, an arrow pointing down
beats.label: RAW ISN'T AUTOMATICALLY BETTER
beats.narration: And you know that raw is not automatically better. Sometimes it is worse.

beats.visual: A pan with every future tomato being cooked the new way
beats.label: EVERY TOMATO AFTER THIS
beats.narration: That one idea changes how you cook every tomato from now on.

beats.visual: A comment box with three tomato options and a reply badge
beats.label: TELL ME
beats.narration: Tell me in the comments how you eat tomatoes. Raw, cooked, or both.

beats.visual: A stack of comment cards with reply badges and a ready pen
beats.label: I READ THEM
beats.narration: I read every single one, and I reply to the interesting ones.

beats.visual: A mystery vegetable under a spotlight with a question mark
beats.label: NEXT VIDEO
beats.narration: In the next video I am going after another vegetable we all cook wrong.

beats.visual: A kitchen counter with the mystery vegetable, shrivelled and overcooked
beats.label: OVERCOOKED
beats.narration: It is in your kitchen right now, and almost everyone overcooks it.

beats.visual: The mystery vegetable with a famous compound name fading in behind it
beats.label: YOU KNOW THIS ONE
beats.narration: And the compound it destroys is one you have definitely heard of.
